expectation: Membrane rings on scattered small lymphocytes: CD8+ intraepithelial lymphocytes in the gut epithelium and resident T cells in the lamina propria. A few DCs. Fairly common in mucosa, sitting as discrete cells along crypts and villi. Mostly CD8a+.
observed: A: haze over the whole section, the bare slide and the label arrow, brightest in muscle, folds and edges. B: diffuse streaks. C: a glowing rim around a lumen. D: a soft blur, no ringed cells. E: CD103 forms continuous bands and blobs that miss most CD8a+ cells.
why: The signal follows tissue texture, muscle, edges and autofluorescence, not discrete membrane-ringed cells, and in row E it rarely lands on the clearly stained CD8a+ cells.
notes: CD103 lights the whole section, the empty slide and the muscle, and outlines lumens in continuous bands. Row E shows well-stained CD8a+ cells, but the CD103 signal mostly lies beside them rather than on them. No convincing CD103+ cell population.
